primary_goals: Strict muscle-up on rings for 5 clean reps
maintenance_goals: Keep my front lever, currently advanced tuck
equipment: Outdoor calisthenics park: pull-up bars, dip bars, rings on a fixed frame, parallettes, a weight belt that takes plates up to 50 kg, resistance bands. No barbell, no rack, no machines, no bench, no box.
current_numbers:
Weighted pull-up: 32 kg x 3
Weighted dip: 45 kg x 3
Strict ring muscle-up: 2 clean reps
Ring dip: 12 reps
Advanced tuck front lever: 12 s
Tuck planche: 15 s
Advanced tuck planche: 6 s
Handstand against wall: 60 s
Freestanding handstand: 8 s
Pistol squat: 8 each leg
Wall handstand push-up: 6 reps to a folded towel
Freestanding handstand push-up: none yet
Currently 5 sessions a week, all calisthenics
injuries: Left elbow gets sore after high-volume straight-arm work; settles in two days and has never stopped training. No pain in bent-arm work at all.

pain.description: Occasional left medial elbow ache after heavy straight-arm days
pain.character: dull, localised to the inner elbow
pain.tolerated_movements: All bent-arm pulling and pressing is tolerated including weighted work. High-volume straight-arm holds back to back on consecutive days are not.

notes: Two primary goals that pull in different directions: the ring muscle-up is a skill and the weighted pull-up is maximal strength, and both are bent-arm pulling. The straight-arm work (planche, front lever) is secondary and maintenance and must not be allowed to eat the elbow's recovery budget or the bent-arm progression. There is no barbell and no machine of any kind: if a session depends on one it will not happen. He can add external load only through the belt or a band.

clarification_answers.benchmark_handstand_pushup: Wall handstand push-up 6 reps to a folded towel; no freestanding handstand push-up yet
clarification_answers.equipment_load_ceiling: Weight belt that takes plates up to 50 kg; bands for assistance only
clarification_answers.adherence_exclusions: None. He will do anything the park allows.
